answer: The cheapest real defence: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because basalt only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, copper is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any sable approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
